title: Inside a streamed run: a tool call in pieces, then the answer in pieces
objectives: Tell apart the events for what the model writes and the events for what the agent runs.
Say when the usage of a streamed run is complete.

steps.title: The learner's question
steps.payload_excerpt: Do I need an umbrella in San Francisco today?

annotation.why: A streamed run starts like any other run: one prompt, then a loop of model requests.

steps.title: Request 1 to the model
steps.summary: The agent sends the message history and the tool list. The reply comes back as events.

annotation.why: With a streamed run the reply is not one object. It is a stream of events, one part at a time.

checkpoint.prompt: The model's reply to request 1 is a tool call, and it is streaming in. Which event do you see first?
checkpoint.explanation: The reply arrives as parts. A PartStartEvent opens the tool-call part. FunctionToolCallEvent comes later, when the agent is about to run your function.

steps.title: The model streams a call to get_forecast
steps.summary: A PartStartEvent opened a tool-call part. A PartDeltaEvent carried the rest of the arguments.

annotation.why: This is the model writing, not your code running. The arguments are only usable once the part ends.

steps.title: FunctionToolCallEvent: the agent runs get_forecast
steps.summary: The model's call is complete. Now the agent calls your function.

annotation.why: The Part events described the model writing the call. This event is your function about to run.

steps.title: FunctionToolResultEvent: the tool answered
steps.summary: get_forecast returned a value. The agent will send it to the model.

annotation.why: The result goes into the history and the next model request streams a new reply.

steps.title: Request 2 to the model
steps.summary: The agent sends the message history and the tool list. The reply comes back as events.

annotation.why: With a streamed run the reply is not one object. It is a stream of events, one part at a time.

steps.title: PartStartEvent: a text part opens
steps.summary: The first piece of text arrives inside the start event.

annotation.why: PartStartEvent carries the first piece of a new part. Later pieces arrive as PartDeltaEvent.

steps.title: FinalResultEvent: this reply is the answer
steps.summary: The agent has seen enough to know this response is the final result.

annotation.why: run_stream stops at the first output that matches the output type. This event marks that point.

steps.title: PartDeltaEvent: the rest of the text arrives in pieces
steps.summary: Each piece is a PartDeltaEvent. A PartEndEvent closes the part.
steps.payload_excerpt: 'bring an umbrella: ' | 'rain is forecast ' | 'in San Francisco today.'

annotation.why: A delta holds only the new piece, never the text so far. Add the pieces up yourself, or let stream_text do it.

checkpoint.prompt: All the text has arrived. If you read the run's usage right now, do you have the final total?
options: Yes, the answer is complete so the total is complete
No, trust the total only when the run is finished
No, usage is only counted for tool calls
checkpoint.explanation: The run is not finished until AgentRunResultEvent. A total read mid-stream is partial, so read usage at the end.

steps.title: AgentRunResultEvent: the run is finished
steps.summary: The last event carries the finished run, with its output and total usage.
steps.payload_excerpt: Yes, bring an umbrella: rain is forecast in San Francisco today.

annotation.why: Read usage here or after the stream ends. Earlier totals are partial. FunctionModel estimates tokens, so no API key was needed.

takeaways: run_stream_events is an async context manager. It yields every event of the whole run and ends with AgentRunResultEvent.
Part events show what the model is writing. FunctionTool events show what the agent runs.
Read usage when the run is finished. A total read mid-stream is partial.
